newsitem.title: FRANCE: Fresh wave of attacks in Corsica, no one injured.
newsitem.headline: Fresh wave of attacks in Corsica, no one injured.

text.p: Suspected Corsican separatists fired shots at a gendarmerie barracks and set off four bombs on the island overnight, French police said on Tuesday.

No casualties were reported in the attacks on the barracks in Figari and offices belonging to the AXA insurance company in Ajaccio, the shipping company SNCM in Ile Rousse, the hunters' federation in Bastia and the holiday villa of perfume company head Georges Guerlain.
Gendarmes said they counted 26 bullet impacts on the gates of their barracks.
The "Historic Wing" of the Corsican National Liberation Front (FLNC) claimed responsibility for the machinegunning of the gendarmerie barracks, the latest in a series of such attacks.
A statement from the underground group said the action was meant as a warning "against all useless provocations".
The group also claimed responsibility for the bomb attack against the home of industrialist Georges Guerlain of Guerlain perfumes, which it accused of "speculation".

The separatist guerrilla group has staged a two-decade-old bombing campaign in Corsica. It recently embarked on a showdown with the Paris government, which has pledged to restore law and order on the French Mediterranean island.
